junction.name: Geary Boulevard & Divisadero Street, San Francisco

claims.text: Geary Boulevard & Divisadero Street had 24 injury crashes in police records since 2021-10-31: 0 people killed.
These counts are Geary Boulevard & Divisadero Street's own: the city's record places 11 of the 35 records within 100 m at another intersection or street, and they are left out.
At the U.S. DOT's values that harm costs about $1.6 million a year.
No crash pattern here stands out against the city's worst crash locations.

This corner got painted safety zones in 2018. Across the city: at 96 sites the change in pedestrian injury crashes (+2%, 95% interval -20% to +34%) could be zero. The city's own record neither shows it worked nor rules it out, so repeating it here rests on other evidence.

This corner got continental crosswalks in 2020. Across the city: at 780 sites the change in pedestrian injury crashes (+4%, 95% interval -25% to +33%) could be zero. The city's own record neither shows it worked nor rules it out, so repeating it here rests on other evidence.
The city's painted safety zones: not shown (at 96 sites the change in pedestrian injury crashes (+2%, 95% interval -20% to +34%) could be zero); a second run of the same design on 780 sites agrees.
Backplates with Retroreflective Borders would avoid about 0.7 crashes a year (CMF 1410, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites; evidence: the record FHWA cites), worth $247,000 a year.

Yellow Change Intervals would avoid about 0.4 crashes a year (CMF 4219, the more conservative of the two middle records of 4; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $128,000 a year; check on site: the current yellow plus all-red time is below the ITE recommended practice.
The San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency (SFMTA) is responsible for Divisadero Street, Geary Boulevard (no route reference, so presumed a city street).
A request letter to the San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency (SFMTA) is ready to draft from these facts.
